title: Smoked Turkey Breast for the Crew

shortDescription: Herb-brined turkey breast with cranberry-mustard glaze for ten
subtitle: Herb-brined turkey breast with cranberry-mustard glaze for ten
description: Bone-in turkey breasts get a simple herb brine, then smoke low and slow until juicy and sliceable. A bright cranberry-mustard glaze finishes on the smoker for color without burning the lean meat.

steps.title: Build the brine
steps.instruction: Dissolve salt and brown sugar in 1 gallon cold water with thyme and garlic. Submerge turkey breasts and refrigerate 8–12 hours so seasoning penetrates evenly.

steps.title: Dry and season
steps.instruction: Remove breasts from brine, pat completely dry, and rub with olive oil, smoked paprika, and black pepper until the surface looks matte and evenly coated.

steps.title: Smoke low and slow
steps.instruction: Heat smoker to 225°F with fruit wood. Place breasts skin-side up and smoke until internal temperature reaches 150°F in the thickest part, about 2–2.5 hours. Target oven/smoker temperature: 225°F.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Whisk mustard with cranberry sauce. Brush over breasts during the final 15 minutes until internal temp hits 165°F and glaze sets glossy without scorching. Target oven/smoker temperature: 225°F.

steps.title: Rest and slice for service
steps.instruction: Tent with foil and rest 15 minutes. Slice against the grain into half-inch portions. Hold covered at 165°F with a tablespoon of broth per pan until the crew lines up.

proTips: Pull at 165°F—turkey dries fast if you chase higher numbers on lean breast meat.
Use a water pan in the smoker to keep the environment humid and the bark from cracking.
Save pan drippings, skim fat, and whisk into the glaze for a richer service sauce.
tonightSpread: Sliced turkey on a hotel pan with extra glaze, soft rolls, and quick pickles on the side.
Simple green salad with lemon vinaigrette to cut the richness of the smoked glaze.
leftovers: Chop into smoked turkey club sandwiches with bacon and sharp cheddar.
Dice and fold into a creamy turkey tetrazzini bake for the next shift lunch.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Turkey breast feels lighter than brisket but still reads as a special smoke night. It slices fast on the line, portions evenly, and reheats without turning stringy when held properly.
mealPrepNotes: Brine breasts up to 24 hours ahead in labeled cambros. Pat completely dry before smoking so the skin sets instead of steaming. Hold sliced turkey at 165°F max in a covered hotel pan with a splash of broth.
